concepts.def: Oneness of God; the central doctrine of Islam expressed in the shahada.
Declaration of faith: 'There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God'.
Ritual prayer performed five times daily facing the Kaaba in Mecca.
Annual obligatory charitable giving, typically 2.5% of qualifying wealth.
Fasting from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan.
Pilgrimage to Mecca undertaken by Muslims able to do so once in a lifetime.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sunni Islam articulates six articles: belief in God (tawhid), in angels (malaika), in revealed books (kutub, including Torah, Psalms, Gospel and Qur'an), in prophets (anbiya, ending with Muhammad), in the Last Day (akhirah) and in divine decree (qadar). Shia Islam organises beliefs slightly differently, emphasising imamate.

The Five Pillars structure Muslim practice: shahada (witness), salah (prayer five times a day at dawn, noon, afternoon, sunset and night), zakat (almsgiving), sawm (fasting in Ramadan) and hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca). Ramadan culminates in Eid al-Fitr; Hajj concludes with Eid al-Adha.

Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan with prayer, communal meals and zakat al-fitr to ensure all can celebrate. Eid al-Adha commemorates the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son and coincides with the Hajj. Both reinforce community and care for the poor.
